chunks: Sama'ah ibn Mihran narrated that he said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man among us has something by which he sustains himself, while he has a debt upon him. Should he feed his dependents with it until Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, brings him ease so that he may repay his debt, or should he borrow burdening himself in the corruption of the times and the hardship of earnings, or should he accept charity?
So he عليه السلام said: He should repay his debt with what he has, and he should not consume the wealth of the people unless he has what he can repay to them.
Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, says: “And do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly.”

key_terms.أَمْوَالَ النَّاسِ: The property or wealth belonging to other people.
key_terms.بِالْبَاطِلِ: Wrongfully, unjustly, or without rightful cause.
key_terms.بِمَيْسَرَةٍ: With ease or financial relief after hardship.
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: A debt or financial obligation owed to another person.
key_terms.عِيَالَهُ: His dependents or family members whom he supports.
key_terms.يَسْتَقْرِضُ: He borrows or takes a loan.

ai.seo_question: Should a debtor use what he has to feed his family first, or repay his debt immediately?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal and ethical ruling on debt: a person who possesses enough to repay what he owes should prioritize settling the debt rather than continuing to use those funds for maintenance through borrowing or other means. It also warns against taking or using the wealth of others without having the capacity to return it, grounding the ruling in the Qur'anic prohibition against consuming wealth unjustly.
